narration: Zelle is built into almost every major banking app — looks totally safe. But there's a legal trap inside it, and if someone tricks you into sending money, your bank owes you absolutely nothing.
visual: Phone with Zelle app on screen, animated thief hand reaching through the screen grabbing a money bag. Red ALERT badge pulses. 'ZERO PROTECTION' text appears below phone.

narration: Last year Americans lost 1.9 billion dollars to peer-to-peer payment scams. That's more than all ATM fraud combined — and almost no one got their money back.
visual: Animated bar chart growing to show $1.9B. Dollar coins fall into frame. Counter climbs from $0 to $1.9B. Light background with bold red bar filling up.

narration: Here's the thing — federal law only covers transactions you didn't authorize. The second a scammer tricks you into sending money yourself, banks legally call it authorized. They owe you zero.
visual: Left column: credit card with green checkmark and '60-day dispute / Federal Law (Reg E)'. Right column: Zelle phone with large red X and 'ZERO days / No Protection'. Dark background, VS divider.

narration: The most common setup: a fake text says your account's been compromised. A scammer posing as your bank walks you through 'protecting' your funds — by sending them to a 'secure' account. Yours.
visual: Phone screen showing a fake 'Your Bank Security' text conversation — messages appear one by one. Final message shows red 'SEND $3,247 via Zelle'. Warning triangle pulses at bottom.

narration: Credit cards give you 60 days to dispute any charge — that's guaranteed by federal law. Zelle, Venmo, CashApp — zero days, zero protection. Scammers specifically ask for Zelle for exactly this reason.
visual: Side-by-side: left shows credit card icon with '60-DAY PROTECTION' badge in green. Right shows Zelle phone with red '$0 PROTECTION'. Stats appear below: '87% of scams specify Zelle', 'Under 3% recovery rate'.

narration: Rule one: never Zelle someone you haven't met face-to-face. Rule two: your real bank will never ask you to send Zelle. And if you've been scammed, file a complaint with the CFPB immediately.
visual: Green shield SVG centered. Three rule cards spring in one by one: RULE 1 (never Zelle a stranger), RULE 2 (banks never ask for Zelle), RULE 3 (CFPB complaint). CTA slides up: 'FOLLOW FOR DAILY MONEY TRAPS'.
